items.title: Integrated Multi-omics Reveals Molecular Signatures of Rett Syndrome, Informing Future Biomarker Discovery.
items.summary: Journal: Molecular neurobiology. Abstract: Rett syndrome (RTT) is a severe neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by pathogenic variants in the X-linked methyl-CpG-binding protein 2 (MECP2) gene. Despite numerous clinical trials being conducted, there are limited disease-modifying options available for individuals with RTT. This paucity of effective treatments can in part be attributed to the lack of clinically useful biomarkers that can objectively assess treatment response. Moreover, diagnosis of RTT continues to be clinical, when clinical manifestations are apparent, precluding early therapeutic approaches. Thus, clinical biomarkers of disease stage could improve diagnosis and enable real-time monitoring of response to treatment, providing the earliest possible indications of therapeutic efficacy. Given MeCP2's role as a key regulator of gene transcription, we used an untargeted omics approach to evaluate transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic profiles in blood from individuals with RTT (n = 9) and age- and sex-matched controls (n = 8). In addition to characterising differential expression at each omic layer, to understand the shared biology and coordinated molecular signals across all omic datasets, we used the unsupervised machine learning framework Multi-Omics Factor Analysis version 2 (MOFA2). The individual omic data consisted of a robust upregulation of genes involved in ribosomal structure and translation together with a downregulation in vesicle trafficking genes. An upregulation in ribosomal machinery and mitochondrial function together with a concomitant downregulation of critical epigenetic regulators, immune-signalling molecules, and cytoskeletal structural anchors was observed in the proteomics, which was supported by the phosphoproteomics. Notably, plasma metabolomics pointed towards alterations in energy substrates and lipid/cholesterol handling, suggesting systemic downstream consequences of primary intracellular disturbances. The integrated MOFA2 data supported the individual omic data revealing a central disease axis principally shaped by the proteome and transcriptome and supported by the metabolome and phosphoproteome, identifying potential biomarkers, including latent biological processes that distinguish RTT from controls (Latent Factor 1) and correlates of clinical severity (Latent Factor 2). Overall, our data reveal a distinctive 'disease state' molecular signature that distinguishes individuals with RTT from controls, where the findings in RTT blood cells are consistent with previously reported altered translational and mitochondrial function and disrupted chromatin regulation, cytoskeletal dynamics, and metabolic signalling. Our integrated multi-omics analyses revealed that PBMC's LTN1, ATRX, CHD8, SPTB, DMTN, PRF1, CD40LG, and PTPRCAP and plasma glutamate are the most promising disease-state (complementary diagnostic) candidate biomarkers while sphingomyelin, RTN3, and MMP1 appear to be the most suitable biomarkers of disease severity. items.headline: Multi-omics reveals molecular signatures of Rett syndrome for biomarker discovery
items.brief: Rett syndrome (RTT), caused by MECP2 mutations, lacks effective treatments partly due to absent biomarkers for disease stage and treatment response. Using untargeted transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic profiling of blood from RTT patients and controls, this study characterizes molecular differences that may inform biomarker development. The integrated multi-omics approach highlights pathways disrupted in RTT, providing a foundation for objective clinical assessment and monitoring.
items.why: This work applies multi-omics profiling to a neurodevelopmental disorder, exemplifying how integrated molecular data can identify biomarkers, a key goal in computational genomics and epigenomics.

items.title: BEND 2.0: Benchmarking the Capabilities Needed to Design DNA
items.summary: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to propose DNA sequences and edits. But successful design requires capabilities that current benchmarks do not measure. Here we introduce BEND 2.0 (BENchmark for DNA language models), which tests how well models predict the effects of DNA changes and whether these predictions can guide sequence design. Across eight tasks built on five experimental datasets, we find that model choice and how representations are accessed both affect performance. Linear readouts fitted to frozen representations can match or exceed models' native outputs, and functional post-training substantially improves the models' capabilities. Linear readouts transfer well across experimental assays and genes, suggesting that models capture functional patterns beyond the data used to fit individual predictors. At the same time, strong prediction of average effects can conceal weaker prediction of context-specific effects, and accurate prediction of combined mutation effects does not imply accurate prediction of their interactions. In design tasks, model predictions can reduce the number of candidates needed to find a desired response, but still leave substantial room for better design choices, particularly for context-specific and multi-cell objectives. Our benchmark reveals that genomic models now display signs of general utility but have yet to saturate on performance in even simple tasks.
items.headline: BEND 2.0 benchmark tests DNA language models for design capabilities
items.brief: BEND 2.0 is a benchmark suite assessing DNA foundation models on predicting effects of DNA changes and guiding sequence design across eight tasks from five experimental datasets. It finds that model choice and representation access affect performance, with linear readouts on frozen representations sometimes outperforming native outputs. Functional post-training improves capabilities, but strong average effect prediction may mask weaker context-specific and interaction effect predictions. Model predictions can guide sequence design but with limitations.
items.why: BEND 2.0 rigorously evaluates DNA language models on functional prediction and design tasks, directly relevant to computational genomics and biological foundation models.
items.korean: BEND 2.0은 DNA 언어 모델의 기능 예측과 설계 능력을 평가하는 벤치마크이다.

items.title: Rethinking One Gene, One Token: Transcriptome-Aware Tokenization for Single-Cell Foundation Models
items.summary: Single-cell foundation models typically treat each gene as a token, which is both costly and wasteful. A cell can express thousands of genes, so one token per gene makes self-attention expensive, yet many of these genes are detected at low levels and carry too little signal to deserve a token of their own. Genes that are expressed together could instead share a token, leaving separate tokens for genes that stand out. We introduce scTAT (Transcriptome-Aware Tokenization), which pairs a gene-set vocabulary with a per-cell tokenizer. The vocabulary holds overlapping gene sets that recur with stable relative expression across the pretraining corpus. Using these sets raises two difficulties. First, which genes should share a token depends on the cell, whereas existing multi-gene tokens fix the grouping in advance. Second, gene sets of different sizes must be compared with single genes on a common scale. The tokenizer therefore decides per cell, letting gene sets and single genes compete for token positions under an expression score normalized by the square root of set size. Training still reconstructs individual genes, so predictions stay at gene resolution. In frozen-embedding cell-type annotation, scTAT matches the strongest one-gene-per-token model with half the token budget. Its advantage over one-gene-per-token models at the same budget grows as the budget shrinks and the tokenizer assigns more positions to gene sets. Encoding the same genes with gene-set tokens also nearly halves the Transformer's matrix-multiplication cost. These results show that a token need not hold exactly one gene: when the tokenizer decides per cell which genes share a token, a fixed budget covers more of each transcriptome at no cost in annotation accuracy.
items.headline: Transcriptome-aware tokenization reduces cost in single-cell foundation models
items.brief: Single-cell foundation models usually treat each gene as a token, which is computationally expensive and inefficient due to many low-expression genes. scTAT introduces transcriptome-aware tokenization by grouping co-expressed genes into overlapping gene sets that compete with single genes for token positions per cell, normalizing expression scores by set size. This dynamic per-cell tokenization reduces token count and computational cost while preserving informative gene expression patterns for model pretraining.
items.why: This method innovatively reduces tokenization complexity in single-cell foundation models, improving scalability and efficiency in computational genomics.
items.korean: scTAT은 단일 세포 모델에서 유전자 토큰화를 효율적으로 개선한다.

items.title: Cortical spreading depression on Riemannian 2-manifolds: eikonal-curvature analysis and sulcal trapping.
items.summary: Journal: Cognitive neurodynamics. Abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) is a slowly propagating wave of near-complete neuronal depolarization underlying migraine aura and implicated in stroke, traumatic brain injury, and subarachnoid hemorrhage. Existing reaction-diffusion models of CSD treat the cortex as a flat Euclidean domain, ignoring its highly folded, individually variable geometry. We develop a fully covariant FitzHugh-Nagumo (FHN) reaction-diffusion system on a smooth compact Riemannian 2-manifold [Formula: see text] representing the cortical sheet, in which the Euclidean Laplacian is replaced by the Laplace-Beltrami operator [Formula: see text]. Three mathematical results are established: (i) local and global well-posedness in [Formula: see text] together with positive invariance of the physiological region via parabolic semigroup theory; (ii) a curvature-corrected eikonal relation [Formula: see text], in which the wavefront speed is modulated by the geodesic curvature of the front; and (iii) a sulcal-trapping theorem giving an explicit criterion under which an excitable wave entering a sulcus (negative Gauss curvature region) remains confined to it. Numerically, we develop two complementary solvers: a discrete exterior calculus (DEC) scheme on triangulated surfaces using the cotangent Laplacian with implicit-explicit (IMEX) time-stepping, and a physics-informed neural network (PINN) surrogate that evaluates [Formula: see text] via the closest-point projection of the ambient Euclidean Laplacian. The PINN framework supports both forward simulation and the inverse identification of excitability fields from sparse observations, and a noise-ablation study quantifies its practical identifiability. The parameters of the slow subsystem and of the coupling functions are inherited from our published, cohort-calibrated thalamocortical model, which was calibrated against 67 paired-pulse somatosensory evoked potential (SEP) recordings from nine analysable animals of a cohort of 14 male Wistar rats (1, 233 sweeps) acquired in the Neuroscience Laboratory of Gazi University, with CSD induced by topical KCl application. We validate convergence on [Formula: see text] with the spectral ground-truth [Formula: see text], exhibit a propagating ring wave with a refractory tail, and verify the eikonal-curvature prediction across two orders of magnitude in geodesic curvature, including the leading correction due to the recovery variable; a mesh-convergence study yields explicit resolution requirements for evaluating the trapping criterion on MRI-derived cortical surfaces.
items.headline: Riemannian FitzHugh-Nagumo model explains cortical spreading depression wave dynamics
items.brief: This study models cortical spreading depression (CSD), a wave of neuronal depolarization linked to migraine aura and brain injury, on smooth Riemannian 2-manifolds representing cortical geometry. Replacing the Euclidean Laplacian with the Laplace-Beltrami operator, the authors prove well-posedness, derive curvature-corrected eikonal relations showing wavefront speed modulation by geodesic curvature, and establish criteria for sulcal trapping of waves. This geometric approach captures effects of cortical folding on CSD propagation.
items.why: It rigorously integrates cortical geometry into reaction-diffusion modeling of neural phenomena, advancing computational neuroscience and mathematical modeling of brain dynamics.
items.korean: 뇌 피질의 곡률을 고려한 확산 모델로 편두통 관련 신경파를 설명했다.

items.title: Young children engage in choice-relative moral reasoning.
items.summary: Journal: Journal of experimental child psychology. Abstract: A central challenge in moral reasoning is evaluating actions not only by their outcomes, but also by the alternatives that were available at the time of choice. The present study examined whether preschool-age children engage in this form of choice-relative moral reasoning. Using a child-friendly version of the trolley problem, 3- to 5-year-old children (N = 124, 51% girls) judged a protagonist who moved a barrier to protect three children's cookies from being eaten by a mean squirrel. Children typically judged this action as morally good when no better alternative was available, even when it caused harm to another child. However, they judged the same action as morally bad when a non-harmful alternative was available but not chosen. These findings suggest that preschool-age children evaluate actions in light of available alternatives rather than solely on the basis of outcomes. Thus, even young children appear to consider what else could have been done when making moral judgments.
items.headline: Preschool children use choice-relative moral reasoning considering alternatives
items.brief: Using a child-friendly trolley problem, 3- to 5-year-olds judged a protagonist's action of moving a barrier to protect cookies. Children rated the action as morally good when no better alternative existed, even if harm occurred, but as morally bad when a non-harmful alternative was available but not chosen. This indicates preschoolers evaluate actions relative to available alternatives, not just outcomes, demonstrating early development of choice-relative moral reasoning.
items.why: This study provides rigorous experimental evidence that young children incorporate counterfactual alternatives in moral judgments, informing evolutionary psychology and cognitive development.
items.korean: 유아들도 선택 가능한 대안을 고려해 도덕 판단을 한다는 것을 보여주었다.
items.evidence_note: Preprint-level caution: behavioral study with young children; interpretations should consider developmental variability.

items.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
items.summary: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.
items.headline: Calabi-Yau dataset catalyzes AI-assisted mathematical discovery
items.brief: Celebrating 50 years since Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture, this article reviews how the Calabi-Yau manifold dataset has united mathematicians and physicists and recently attracted machine learning and AI methods. It recounts the growth of AI-assisted mathematics over the past decade and highlights 2026 as a landmark year for dramatic advances in mathematical discovery aided by AI, emphasizing the transformative impact of computational approaches on pure mathematics.
items.why: It documents the integration of computational genomics-inspired AI methods into deep mathematical research, illustrating cross-disciplinary innovation and foundation model applications.
items.korean: 칼라비-야우 다양체 데이터셋이 AI 기반 수학 연구 발전을 촉진했다.
